To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
glucose increases significantly IRI release from synaptosomes isolated form rat brain.
glucose stimulates the release of IRI in brain synaptosomes and the effect is mediated by glucose metabolism.
glucose stimulates insulin release from synaptosomes isolated form rat brain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an in vitro model for studying the mechanism of brain insulin release.
a study of the mechanism of glucose-induced IRI release in synaptosomes.
the development of a model of insulin release in the central nervous system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
glucose is a stimulatory agent for IRI release in synaptosomes and that this release may be mediated, at least in part, by glucose metabolism.
insulin is released from the brain and this is a glucose-dependent process.
the brain is able to secrete insulin and that the insulin is stored in a releasable pool in the brain synaptosomes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

glucose stimulates insulin release in synaptosomes, that this effect is partially dependent upon glucose metabolism, and that the insulin released in response to glucose is immunologically similar to insulin from pancreatic islets.
the brain synaptosomes are a good model to study the mechanism of insulin action in the brain.
the glucose-induced release from synaptosomes is mediated by the same mechanism as in pancreatic beta cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the brain can release insulin and it does so in response to a stimulus.
glucose is a signal for insulin release from synaptosomes.
synaptosomes can be used as an in vitro model to study the mechanisms underlying glucose-induced insulin release in the brain.
